ei.title: Practice 01 — 윤리적 기준이 소비자들의 소비성향에 미치는 영향
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본2

fullPassage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were ②<u>relative</u> homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers ①<u>conducted</u> a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were ③<u>willing</u> to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in ④<u>shaping</u> those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② relative(X) / relatively(O): homogeneous(형용사)를 수식하려면 부사 relatively가 와야 한다. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① conducted: 'researchers conducted a series of experiments' — 주어에 호응하는 과거동사로 올바른 어법
❌ ② relative → relatively: 'relatively homogeneous'에서 형용사 homogeneous를 수식하는 자리이므로 부사 relatively가 필요함. 형용사 relative는 형용사를 수식할 수 없어 어법 오류
✅ ③ willing: 'were willing to pay' — be willing to + V 관용 구문으로 올바른 어법
✅ ④ shaping: 'in shaping those results' — 전치사 in 뒤에 동명사 형태로 올바른 어법
det.tip: 형용사 수식에는 부사가 필요합니다. relatively(부사) + homogeneous(형용사). relative(형용사)로 쓰면 형용사가 형용사를 수식하는 어법 오류.

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers ①<u>conducting</u> a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items ②<u>had been made</u> using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers ③<u>were willing</u> to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① conducting(X) / conducted(O): 주어 researchers의 본동사 자리이므로 과거형 conducted가 와야 한다. ← 정답
det.analysis:
❌ ① conducting → conducted: 'researchers conducting a series of experiments'에서 conducting은 현재분사로 주절 동사 역할을 할 수 없음. 문장의 본동사 자리에는 과거형 conducted가 필요
✅ ② had been made: 'items had been made using high ethical standards' — 과거(told) 기준 이전 시제를 나타내는 과거완료수동으로 올바른 어법
✅ ③ were willing: 'consumers were willing to pay' — be willing to 구문으로 올바른 어법
✅ ④ rewarded: 'rewarded the ethical companies' — 과거동사로 올바른 어법
det.tip: 현재분사(-ing)는 문장의 본동사가 될 수 없습니다. 주어 researchers의 본동사 자리에는 과거형 conducted가 필요합니다.

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product ①<u>if the product were</u> relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? ②<u>To find out</u>, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much ③<u>further</u> in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and ④<u>punished the unethical ones with more bigger discounts</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ more bigger(X) / bigger(O): 비교급에 more를 붙이는 이중 비교급은 어법 오류이다. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① if the product were: 가정법 과거에서 be동사는 주어에 관계없이 were를 사용하는 정상 어법
✅ ② To find out: 목적을 나타내는 부정사구로 'To find out, researchers conducted'에서 올바른 어법
✅ ③ further: 'went much further in the other direction' — much가 비교급 further를 강조하는 정상 구조
❌ ④ more bigger → bigger: 비교급 bigger에 more를 추가하면 이중 비교급이 되어 어법 오류. bigger만 써야 함
det.tip: 이중 비교급은 금지됩니다. more + -er 형태는 불가. more bigger(×) → bigger(○), more + 원급(beautiful → more beautiful은 가능).

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively ①<u>homogeneous</u>. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a ②<u>slight</u> premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a ③<u>modest</u> discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior ④<u>rewarded</u> the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ modest(X) / steep(O): 비윤리 제품은 '큰 폭의' 할인을 요구하므로 modest(적당한)로 바꾸면 의미가 반전된다. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① homogeneous: 'relatively homogeneous' — 제품이 동질적이라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② slight: 'pay a slight premium' — 윤리 제품에 약간의 프리미엄 지불. 뒤의 steep discount와 대비되어 적절
❌ ③ modest → steep: 원문 'buy unethically made products only at a steep discount' — steep(가파른, 큰 폭의)이 맞음. modest(적당한)로 바꾸면 '작은 할인에도 비윤리 제품을 산다'는 의미가 되어 소비자의 강한 처벌 반응(큰 할인 요구)과 반대
✅ ④ rewarded: 'rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums' — 윤리 기업에 보상하는 것으로 적절
det.tip: steep = 가파른, 큰 폭의. steep discount = 대폭 할인. modest = 적당한, 소박한. 소비자가 비윤리 제품에 강하게 반응(큰 할인 요구)하는 맥락에 steep이 적합합니다.

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using ②<u>high ethical standards</u> and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight ③<u>premium</u> for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in ④<u>shaping</u> those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and ①<u>rewarded</u> the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ rewarded(X) / punished(O): 비윤리 기업은 더 큰 할인(처벌)을 받아야 하므로 rewarded로 바꾸면 의미가 반전된다. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ④ high ethical standards: 'items had been made using high ethical standards' — 윤리 기준이 높다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② premium: 'pay a slight premium' — 윤리 상품에 추가 금액 지불로 적절
✅ ③ shaping: 'in shaping those results' — 결과를 형성하는 데 역할을 한다는 의미로 적절
❌ ① rewarded → punished: 원문 'punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts'에서 punished(처벌하다)가 맞음. rewarded(보상하다)로 바꾸면 비윤리 기업에 더 큰 보상을 준다는 의미 반전. 앞 문장 'rewarded the ethical companies'와 대조되어 비윤리 기업에는 punished가 맞음
det.tip: reward(보상) ↔ punish(처벌): 윤리 기업은 reward(더 큰 프리미엄), 비윤리 기업은 punish(더 큰 할인 요구). 앞 문장과 대조 구조를 파악하세요.

They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight __________ for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 윤리적으로 만들어진 상품에 소비자들이 약간의 __________을 기꺼이 지불하려 했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① discount: 할인은 비윤리 제품 맥락(steep discount)에 해당하므로 오답
✅ ② premium: 'consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods' — 윤리 상품에 추가 금액 지불 = premium. 정답
❌ ③ refund: 환불은 구매 후 돌려받는 것으로 맥락 불일치
❌ ④ penalty: 벌금은 소비자가 부과받는 개념이 아니므로 맥락 불일치
det.tip: premium = 기본 가격 이상으로 지불하는 추가금. pay a premium for ethical goods = 윤리 제품에 웃돈을 지불하다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 뿐만 아니라, __________이(가) 그 결과를 형성하는 데 큰 역할을 했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ethical standards: 윤리 기준은 실험의 독립변수(처치 조건)이지 '결과를 형성하는 요인' 자리에 맞지 않음
❌ ② product information: 제품 정보는 통제 집단 구분에 사용된 개념으로 결과를 형성한 직접 요인(×)
✅ ③ consumer attitudes: 'consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results' — 소비자 태도/기준이 결과 형성에 영향. 다음 문장 'People with high standards for corporate behavior'가 구체화. 정답
❌ ④ corporate behavior: 기업 행동은 소비자 평가의 대상이지 결과를 형성한 소비자 측 요인(×)
det.tip: 다음 문장 'People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded/punished'가 consumer attitudes의 내용을 구체화합니다.

det.korean: ④번: 통제 집단이 가격 정보도 받지 못했다는 내용은 본문에 없으므로 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 일치: 'showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts'
✅ ② 일치: 'consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods'
✅ ③ 일치: 'told...another group that low standards had been used'
❌ ④ 불일치: 원문 'A control group got no information' — 통제 집단은 윤리 관련 정보를 받지 못했음. '가격 정보도 받지 못했다'는 원문에 없는 과잉 서술로 불일치
det.tip: control group = 실험 처치(윤리 정보 제공)를 받지 않은 집단. 가격 정보 제공 여부는 본문에 언급이 없습니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 윤리적 기준이 소비자의 지불 의향과 구매 행동(프리미엄/할인)에 미치는 영향을 실험으로 검증한 글.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 제품 품질 영향: 실험은 동일 제품을 사용했고 품질은 변수가 아님
✅ ② 윤리적 기준 → 소비자 지불 의향·구매 행동: 본문 전체의 핵심 — 윤리 기준에 따라 소비자가 프리미엄/할인을 달리 결정함. 정답

questions.passage: In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts.
